name: Attentional Selection Circuit
short_description: Combines saliency-driven bottom-up signals with task-relevance top-down biases in winner-take-all competition to select attended target and implement inhibition of return.

components.name: SALIENCY_CALCULATOR
components.description: Computes visual saliency based on stimulus features (luminance, color, motion, orientation contrasts)

components.name: TASK_BIAS_GENERATOR
components.description: Generates task-relevant attentional biases from goal representations

components.name: CURRENT_FIXATION_TRACKER
components.description: Tracks current attentional locus for inhibition of return implementation

components.name: WINNER_TAKE_ALL_SELECT
components.description: Implements biased competition with winner-take-all dynamics and inhibition of return

scope_conditions: Visual scene with multiple candidate targets
Defined task context with relevance structure
key_references: Desimone, R., & Duncan, J. (1995). Neural mechanisms of selective visual attention. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 18, 193–222.
Itti, L., & Koch, C. (2001). Computational modelling of visual attention. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2(3), 194–203.
design_implications: Task-relevant information should be salient or uniquely located; in complex visual environments (forms, dashboards, public signage), distinguish critical elements through color, contrast, or spatial isolation
Attentional capture wastes cognitive resources; minimize irrelevant visual salience (flashing, bright colors, movement) in task-focused contexts
